Subject: SDK install & backpressure checklist for BlueMatter

Hi Samantha — great demo this morning, thanks for walking us through the BlueMatter ingestion use case. Recap + asks below so we can align engineering and commercial next steps.

Quick recap (what we heard)
- Primary flows: user chat + async batch embedding job for search reranker.
- Target peak: ~400 TPS for chat during biz-hours, batch embeddings ~3000 requests/hour (longer tail).
- Security: corporate VPC + KMS for encryption; SOC2 required.
- Concern: graceful degradation during bursts and avoiding double-charging/dup processing.

Open technical items we promised to confirm
1) Auth: preferred long-lived API key vs short-lived signed tokens for SDK install?
2) Routing: single-region vs multi-region routing for EU/US?
3) Rate limits & retry semantics: what are your client-side retry rules today?
4) Idempotency: which operations require dedupe (chat exchange writes vs billing-affecting calls)?

Proposed timescale & next steps
- This week: tech sync to confirm auth + request-id policy (30m)
- Next week: POC SDK install + reference config (we'll provide sample code and an integration-checklist.pdf)
- Week after: load-run (simulated bursts) to validate token bucket / burst policies and proposed Dedicated fallback if needed.

Attachments: [Attachment: integration-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

I'll follow up with an initial proposal for the SDK defaults (auth header names, request-id conventions, client-side backoff) after you confirm your auth preference.

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers and questions from our infra team: 

Auth: we prefer short-lived tokens (rotated) for host-level access; service-to-service calls can use signed tokens. Can your SDK support both without major changes?

Rate expectations: peak chat TPS is likely nearer 500 in our busiest region, but we do have spiky events (marketing pushes). We currently have a client retry policy: 3 attempts, linear backoff 1s -> 2s -> 3s. We're worried that naive retries amplify bursts.

Idempotency: important for chat stream acknowledgement and for runs that consume credits (embeddings). We use an idempotency key header today: X-Idempotency-Key, window ~60s.

Structured output / tooling: for the reranker we want a tool-calling pattern where model can emit a structured JSON with embeddings hints (i.e., field: "reranker_hint"). Are there recommended SDK helpers for structured outputs?

Attached a quick infra diagram for context: [Attachment: bluematter-infra-diagram.png (image/png)]

Thanks — that's helpful context. Below is a concise recommendation tailored to your constraints; happy to expand in the tech sync.

Auth & SDK flows
- Recommendation: short-lived bearer tokens (signed by your KMS-backed service) for client instances + optional API key for service-to-service. SDK supports both: you can set "authProvider": "signed_token" or "api_key" in config.
- Token rotation: 15m TTL tokens with automatic refresh via SDK hook. Token refresh calls are rate-limited and do not count toward per-request quotas.

Routing / regional placement
- Suggest regional endpoints: us-west-2 for US traffic; eu-west-1 for EU. SDK will prefer local endpoint; configure fallback policy: prefer local -> remote (with throttling) -> Dedicated fallback.

Rate limiting & retry strategy (429 handling)
- Client-side: implement a leaky-bucket + request queue with configurable max in-flight (default 50). Use exponential backoff with full-jitter for 429s: base=200ms, cap=10s, attempts=5.
- Server-side headers: Redwood will return Retry-After (s) and a rate-class header X-Rate-Limit-Policy which SDK will inspect to adapt backoff windows.
- For bursts: recommend token-bucket on the client set to your steady-state TPS (e.g., 300) with burst capacity of 2x for short windows; combine with server-side 429 -> SDK backoff.

Idempotency & request IDs
- Use X-Request-Id for tracing (UUID v4). For ops that affect billing or write-state (embeddings ingestion), require X-Idempotency-Key (64-char max) and keep server dedupe window at 120s for embeddings jobs.
- SDK will surface an IdempotencyKey generator (sha256 of payload + timestamp nonce) and allow customers to override.

Structured output / tool calling
- SDK includes a small "tooling" helper that validates model-emitted JSON against a provided schema. For reranker hints, pass a schema with the field "reranker_hint" and the SDK will enforce/serialize it.

Implementation checklist (what we'll provide)
- integration-checklist.pdf (attached)
- SDK sample config (authProvider, region, requestQueue, idempotencyPolicy)
- Small load test harness for us to run together (we'll coordinate run windows)

Operational notes
- Logging: we recommend shipping X-Request-Id to your central tracing and retaining token-refresh logs for 7 days.
- Observability: we can instrument a per-API-key latency breakdown in the Console to help tune bucket sizes.

I'll bring a short proposal and a sample client config to the tech sync. Proposed times: Thu 07/01 09:00 or Thu 07/01 14:00 ET — which works for you?

-Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
